strategy_version: SPY vs V1 / DD Only / Combined DD+Vol (volatility-persistence audit)
dataset: SPY (data/raw/SPY.csv); exp_007 net+gross strategy returns; exp_005 base return

parameters.strategy_fit_warning: strategy GARCH-t fits hit nu~8 (near start), several non-convergent, sq-std-resid Ljung-Box p=0 => GARCH(1,1) misspecified for risk-controlled returns

assumptions: GARCH(1,1) with constant mean; standardized Student-t innovations; MLE via scipy. Persistence compared across market vs raw-base vs risk-controlled strategy returns.
hypothesis: Does volatility persistence differ materially between SPY, raw alpha and risk-controlled variants?
limitations: (1) Strategy GARCH-t fits are numerically unstable (nu pinned ~8, non-convergence, near-unit persistence) and MISSPECIFIED (squared standardized residuals remain autocorrelated), so strategy persistence estimates are not reliable point values. (2) NB03 Monte Carlo fits/resamples already risk-controlled returns directly (method B); it does NOT dynamically replay the drawdown overlay. A faithful dynamic replay (method A) gives LIGHTER tail drawdowns than B. (3) V1 dual-layer overlay not dynamically replayed (DD Only & Combined are, to 1e-15). (4) Near-unit persistence inflates GARCH tail-MDD dispersion.

extra.status: audit complete; no deployment candidate selected or changed
extra.central_question_answer: Persistence is materially higher & less stable for the risk-controlled strategy returns than for SPY, but this largely reflects GARCH(1,1) misspecification on endogenously risk-controlled series, not a clean risk signal.
